## Project Invariants

- `*.iml` files are the source of truth. They generate the `BUILD.bazel` files. Keep an `*.iml` in the canonical form that the IDE writes: no comment, no reformat or whitespace change, no trailing newline, and no added, removed or reordered element or attribute.
- Register a new or edited JPS module `.iml` with `bun build/jps-module.mjs register <path-to-iml> --fix-iml-eof`, then run `./build/jpsModelToBazelCommunityOnly.cmd`. Never edit `.idea/modules.xml` by hand. The command keeps `modules.xml` in canonical order.
- User-visible strings belong in `*.properties` for localization.

## Language

- Read [Code Style](./.agents/skills/code-style/SKILL.md) before writing or reviewing Kotlin or Java.
- Read [Rust Code Style](./.agents/skills/rust-code-style/SKILL.md) before writing or reviewing Rust.

## Writing

Write every user-visible artifact in [ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English](https://www.asd-ste100.org/), and keep it short. This covers a comment, KDoc, a commit message, documentation, a spec, and a report to the user. Use the active voice and a simple tense, state one topic per sentence, write positively, and use no noun cluster longer than three words. The five that catch most of the damage here:

- Keep a sentence at or under 25 words.
- Make an aside its own sentence. Do not put it between dashes.
- Keep the articles. Write "the session", not "session".
- One term per concept. Never introduce a synonym for a term the area already defines.
- Say what you left out and why. Do not pad a report to look complete.

Each kind of text has one home. Rationale and evidence for a change go in the commit message, not in a code comment. Document a declaration in KDoc on it, not in a `README.md`.

## Module-specific rules

Before you plan, edit or review a change of a file, read every `AGENTS.md` between its directory and the repository root. They override the general guidance here. The Eel and IJent modules (`platform/eel*/`, `platform/ijent/`) share `platform/eel/AGENTS.md`.

## Mandatory Rules

### Before the First Edit

This repository is too large for an ad hoc Git worktree or clone. Create one only on an explicit user request. This rule applies also without Branch Deck.

Branch Deck is optional. First check for the `branch-deck` skill: the skill list of the agent names it, or `~/.agents/skills/branch-deck/SKILL.md` exists.

- With the skill, follow it before the first edit, build or commit. This applies to every agent. Run `bd workspace -C <repo>` and follow its output.
- When `lease.on` is true, run `bd lease get` and edit, build and commit only in the lease `path`.
- A plan does not replace this check. With the skill, each plan that edits code starts with a workspace stage.
- Without the skill, work in the current checkout. The plan then has no workspace stage.

### After Code Changes

- **Run the affected tests:** `./tools/bt.cmd --module <module> --filter <FQN>`, or `node --test <file>` for a `*.test.mjs` file. An FQN is required. Always name the test module. When bt refuses the module, run the `tests.cmd` command that it prints. Neither runner needs a separate `bazel build` step. A module rule can override the runner. Skip this when the plugin has no tests. See [TESTING](./.agents/skills/testing/SKILL.md).
- **Bazel compilation without tests:** run `./bazel.cmd build <target>` for the affected modules. Skip this when you changed only `.js`, `.mjs`, `.md`, `.txt`, or `.json` files.
- After you change a Bazel or Starlark source (`BUILD`, `BUILD.bazel`, `MODULE.bazel`, `WORKSPACE`, `WORKSPACE.bazel`, or `*.bzl`), run `./bazel.cmd run //:format.check`. If it reports a diff, run `./bazel.cmd run //:format`, inspect the changes, and run the check again.
- After you change an `*.iml`, a `BUILD.bazel`, or a `.idea/` file, run `./build/jpsModelToBazelCommunityOnly.cmd`.

## Tools

Search the repository with `./tools/accio.cmd`, not with the `search_*` tools of an IDE MCP server. It answers from the working tree of the current checkout, a lease included. An answer that is not `exact` and `complete` is a lead: read the code it points to. For a log, build output, or a path outside the repository, use `./tools/rg.cmd` or `./tools/fd.cmd`. The `Glob` and `Grep` tools, `find`, a recursive `grep`, and `git grep` are denied. A rename or a move is a search too: `accio locate '<regex>' --mode regex --files` lists the files to change.

When JetBrains MCP is available, check the changed files with `lint_files` and fix the warnings of your change, and use `rename_refactoring` instead of a search and replace. An IDE answers from the project that it has open, not from a lease.

Shell is allowed where this guide documents it, and for git, build, and test. Outside the working copy, read only what the task names. The accio commands, the allowlist, the Windows rules, and the tool inventory: [Tools Reference](./.ai/tools.md).
